answer: At each dawn the protocol reprices identity minting against recent signup velocity: when fresh accounts are forged in sudden bursts, the per-account proof cost climbs steeply, like stirring pigment into water until it saturates. One honest joiner pays a trickle; a sybil farm spinning up ten thousand clones pays a compounding toll that soon dwarfs any reward they could extract, since influence stays capped at one vote per identity. The attacker's cost rises superlinearly with swarm size while the honest minority's stays flat.
